newsitem.title: USA: Boston Gas files for reconsideration.
newsitem.headline: Boston Gas files for reconsideration.

text.p: Eastern Enterprises said on Thrusday that its Boston Gas Co unit has filed with the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities a request for reconsideration, clarification and recalculation of the November 29, 1996 order received from the department regarding its rate restructuring proposal.

In its order, the department rejected a previously filed Settlement Agreement that covered several crucial economic and rate design issues and granted an increase in base revenues of only $6.3 million, instead of the $13.0 million agreed to in the settlement.
The settlement was entered into by Boston Gas and representatives of a number of consumer groups, including the Massachusetts attorney general's office.

In the petition filed today, Boston Gas said that the initial rates ordered by the department, when considered in conjunction with the formula and service quality measures, would result in confiscatory returns on investment that would deteriorate over the six-year life of the plan.

Boston Gas also argued that the department's order would have a negative impact on Eastern's incremental investment in the company, would hamper efforts to achieve efficiencies through industry consolidation, would adversely impact the economy and the environment in Massachusetts, and, over the longer term, would result in higher prices for natural gas.
